contentBlocks.text: This week you've learned to read maps. Today: use that to understand why communities around the world look so different!

A place's climate — how hot, cold, wet, or dry it usually is — shapes how the community living there builds homes, grows food, and dresses, connecting back to last week's community framework (people, environment, traditions). A community in a very cold, snowy climate needs homes built to hold in heat and warm clothing, while a community in a hot, dry climate needs homes that stay cool and clothing that protects from strong sun. Describe how you think climate shapes homes or clothing where you live.
You just connected climate to how communities live around the world! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Explain that climate influences how communities build homes and choose clothing
Describe how the child's own local climate shapes homes or clothing in their community
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's map-skills work.
2. Introduce the climate-shapes-communities idea using the cold/hot climate examples, connecting back to last week's people/environment/traditions framework.
3. Have the child describe their own local climate's effect on homes or clothing.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just clothing (a very concrete, personally-experienced example) rather than requiring both homes and clothing
Ready for more: ask the child to describe how climate might also affect what food a community grows or eats
Kept deliberately general — describing climate's effects broadly rather than naming or characterizing specific real communities or ethnic groups, per the platform's content-sensitivity discipline
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended reflection activity — check that the child gives a genuine, locally-grounded example of how climate shapes homes or clothing where they live.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the C3 Framework's Geography dimension (human-environment interaction) at a Grade 3 level, connecting this week's map skills back to last week's community-framework content.
